translation_en: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, from Simak, Abu Zumayl, who said: Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to me: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, who said: When the Prophet of Allah stayed apart from his wives, I entered the mosque and found people striking the ground with pebbles and saying, “The Messenger of Allah has divorced his wives.” This was before they were commanded to observe the veil. Umar said: I resolved to find out about this that day. I went to Aishah and said, “Daughter of Abu Bakr, has it come to this, that you would hurt the Messenger of Allah?” She said, “What business is it of yours, son of al-Khattab? Attend to your own affairs.” I went to Hafsah bint Umar and said, “Hafsah, has it come to this, that you would hurt the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, you know that the Messenger of Allah does not love you. Were it not for me, the Messenger of Allah would have divorced you.” She wept intensely. I asked her, “Where is the Messenger of Allah?” She said, “He is in his room in the upper chamber.” I entered and found Rabah, the Messenger of Allah’s servant, sitting on the threshold of the chamber, with his legs hanging over a hollowed wooden log. It was a trunk on which the Messenger of Allah climbed and descended. I called, “Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah.” Rabah looked toward the room, then at me, but said nothing. I said again, “Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah.” Rabah looked toward the room, then at me, but said nothing. Then I raised my voice and said, “Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of Allah. I think the Messenger of Allah believes I came on Hafsah’s account. By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah orders me to strike her neck, I will strike her neck.” I raised my voice, and he gestured to me to climb up. I entered upon the Messenger of Allah while he was reclining on a mat. I sat down, and he pulled his lower garment around himself; he had nothing else on. The mat had left marks on his side. I looked around the Messenger of Allah’s storeroom and saw only a handful of barley, about a sa‘ measure, and a similar amount of acacia pods in one corner. There was also a water skin hanging up. Umar said: My eyes overflowed with tears. He said, “What makes you weep, son of al-Khattab?” I said, “Prophet of Allah, why should I not weep? This mat has left marks on your side, and this is your storeroom; I see in it only what I see. Yet Caesar and Chosroes live among fruits and rivers, while you are the Messenger of Allah and His chosen one, and this is your storeroom.” He said, “Son of al-Khattab, are you not pleased that the Hereafter is ours and this world is theirs?” I said, “Yes.” Umar said: When I entered upon him, I saw anger on his face. I said, “Messenger of Allah, what is difficult for you about the women? If you have divorced them, Allah is with you, as are His angels, Gabriel, Michael, I, Abu Bakr, and the believers.” I would rarely say something while praising Allah without hoping that Allah would confirm what I said. Then the verse of choice was revealed: “Perhaps, if he divorces you, his Lord will replace you with wives better than you…” Quran 66:5, and, “If you two support one another against him, then Allah is his Protector, as are Gabriel, the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that” Quran 66:4. Aishah bint Abi Bakr and Hafsah had joined together against the other wives of the Prophet. I said, “Messenger of Allah, have you divorced them?” He said, “No.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, I entered the mosque and found the Muslims striking the ground with pebbles and saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah has divorced his wives.’ Shall I go down and tell them that you have not divorced them?” He said, “Yes, if you wish.” I continued speaking to him until the anger left his face and he smiled broadly. He had one of the most beautiful smiles among people. Then the Prophet of Allah descended, and I descended, holding onto the trunk as I climbed down. The Messenger of Allah descended as though he were walking on the ground, without touching it with his hand. I said, “Messenger of Allah, you stayed in the room for twenty-nine days.” He said, “A month can be twenty-nine days.” I stood at the mosque door and called out at the top of my voice, “The Messenger of Allah has not divorced his wives.” This verse was revealed: “When news of security or fear comes to them, they spread it. If they had referred it to the Messenger and those in authority among them, those able to draw conclusions would have known it” Quran 4:83. I was among those who drew the matter out, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse of choice.
